- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.40) — model fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Lag in price correction after spikes — model delays reaction to recent highs, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent volatility and underweights long-term trend, leading to over- or under-forecasting in middle-term horizons.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes — model reacts too aggressively to short-term sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns positive after a dip.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 2025-09-26 to 2025-10-01) — model fails to account for sentiment decay or policy uncertainty.
